Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 102, verses 1–2:

O you who race headlong in a state of heedlessness, O you who, in a state of carelessness, strive for abundance of wealth and children and a plentiful supply of worldly goods, you are surely going to leave all these things behind in this very world. O you who are deceived by the preoccupations of the world, O you who will leave wealth and children behind, O you who are going to a narrow pit, the grave: in the grave there will be no wealth, no children, and there will be no pride or display of superiority there. Awake, and look, and reflect.

﴿Al-hakumut-takathur, hatta zurtumul-maqabir﴾ (102:1–2): "The mutual rivalry for more and more [worldly gain] has distracted you, until you visit the graves." But after the tour of the graves, there is a terrifying scene for you there: in a most severe and forceful manner, their hearts are shaken in this way.

After this, the reality is emphasized so that fear of it may take hold of the hearts.

And now the final blow is struck with such force that even the most heedless of people is roused and becomes alert, and one who is rushing headlong in the direction he faces pauses for a moment and turns his attention to it. Even the comfort of the wealthiest man is clouded: he begins to tremble, and fear over those blessings takes hold of his heart.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 102, verse 8:

You will be asked: how did you acquire these blessings, and where did you spend them? Did you acquire them by obeying Allah and spend them in obedience to Allah, or did you acquire them by disobeying Allah and spend them in disobedience? Did you earn them through lawful means and spend them in lawful causes, or did you earn them through unlawful means and spend them unlawfully? Did you give thanks for these blessings? Did you fulfil their due rights? Did you share them with others in them, or did you keep using them only for yourselves?

These questions will certainly be put to you: how you gathered this wealth, and how you took pride in it. Because of your intoxication and heedlessness, this wealth and these bounties appear light to you, and appear as mere play. But behind them lies a heavy responsibility and a severe accountability.

This Surah, though very brief, is itself its own explanation. It overwhelms human sensibility, takes hold of it, and the human heart and vision appear heavy under its grip. A person who suddenly comprehends the reality of the world, leaves its petty pleasures and low-value priorities, and becomes occupied with thinking about the Hereafter. Meanwhile, ordinary people, whose hearts are free of these realities and effects, are busy sacrificing themselves for these worthless things.

This Surah presents this world in the way that a single second's glimpse appears within a long film.

﴿Alhakumu at-takathur * hatta zurtumu al-maqabir﴾ (102:1-2): "Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you, until you visit the graves." In these few words, a glimpse of the entire worldly life is shown, and then it is wrapped up. Then the film of the eternal and everlasting life begins, and the criminals will carry their burdens for a long age, and even to eternity. This concept is given in a most beautiful style of expression, and the actual reality and the manner of expression become one.

Whoever reads this great, fearsome Surah with understanding, whose effects rise from the earth like a storm, reach the skies, and appear on the distant horizon, whose meanings are very solid and settle deep within the ocean of heart and mind, will find his heart grow heavy. He perceives how long, in terms of its consequences and effects, is this brief flash and glitter of life on this earth. Thus every sensible person sets out on the path of long preparation for the life of the Hereafter, and on this path he becomes sensitive even to small matters.
